characters.name: Ebenezer Scrooge
characters.summary: A cold, miserly London businessman who despises Christmas.

notes.text: Is warned by Marley’s ghost that three spirits will visit him.
Wakes on Christmas morning a changed man, generous and joyful.

characters.name: Jacob Marley
characters.summary: Scrooge’s business partner, dead these seven years.

notes.text: Appears as a ghost, bound in the chain he forged in life.

characters.name: Bob Cratchit
characters.summary: Scrooge’s poorly paid, patient clerk.

characters.name: Fred
characters.summary: Scrooge’s cheerful nephew, who invites him to Christmas dinner every year.

characters.name: Ghost of Christmas Past
characters.summary: A strange, candle-like spirit, both young and old, who shows Scrooge his past.

characters.name: Fan
characters.summary: Scrooge’s affectionate little sister.

characters.name: Mr. Fezziwig
characters.summary: The jovial merchant to whom young Scrooge was apprenticed.

characters.name: Mrs. Fezziwig
characters.summary: Fezziwig’s warm-hearted wife.

characters.name: Dick Wilkins
characters.summary: Scrooge’s fellow apprentice at Fezziwig’s.

characters.name: Belle
characters.summary: The young woman Scrooge once loved.

notes.text: Is later seen happily married with a large family.

characters.name: Ghost of Christmas Present
characters.summary: A jolly green-robed giant who shows Scrooge Christmas as it is being kept that day.

characters.name: Mrs. Cratchit
characters.summary: Bob’s wife, making a brave show of a modest Christmas.

characters.name: Tiny Tim
characters.summary: Bob’s youngest son: small, frail, carrying a crutch, and full of goodwill.

notes.text: The Spirit warns he will die unless the future is altered.
Does not die; Scrooge becomes a second father to him.

characters.name: Martha Cratchit
characters.summary: Bob’s eldest daughter, apprenticed to a milliner.

characters.name: Peter Cratchit
characters.summary: Bob’s son, proud of his father’s borrowed shirt collar.

characters.name: Belinda Cratchit
characters.summary: One of Bob’s daughters.

characters.name: Fred’s wife
characters.summary: Fred’s pretty, laughing wife, Scrooge’s niece by marriage.

characters.name: Topper
characters.summary: A bachelor friend at Fred’s Christmas party.

characters.name: Ghost of Christmas Yet to Come
characters.summary: A silent, hooded phantom who points the way to things to come.

characters.name: Old Joe
characters.summary: A receiver of stolen goods in a squalid rag-and-bone shop.

characters.name: Mrs. Dilber
characters.summary: A laundress who brings a dead man’s belongings to sell.

phases.label: Late business partner
phases.note: Scrooge was his sole executor and mourner; his ghost comes to warn him.

phases.label: Employer & clerk
phases.note: Scrooge begrudges him even a day off at Christmas.

phases.label: A generous employer
phases.note: Scrooge raises his salary and promises to help his family.

phases.label: Reconciled
phases.note: Scrooge turns up for Christmas dinner and is welcomed.

phases.label: Shows him what may come
phases.note: It ends at a neglected grave bearing his own name.

phases.label: Brother & sister
phases.note: She comes to bring him home from school.

phases.label: Master & apprentice
phases.note: His Christmas Eve ball shows Scrooge how little kindness costs.

phases.label: Broken engagement
phases.note: She releases him, saying a golden idol has displaced her in his heart.

phases.label: Father & son
phases.note: Bob carries him home from church on his shoulder.

phases.label: Moved by him
phases.note: Scrooge asks the Spirit whether Tiny Tim will live.

phases.label: A second father
phases.note: Tiny Tim, who did not die, gains a second father in Scrooge.

phases.label: Holds him in contempt
phases.note: She toasts him only for Bob’s sake and the day’s.

phases.label: Friends
phases.note: Topper plays blind man’s buff at the party.

phases.label: Kind stranger
phases.note: In the vision of the future, Fred offers help after the Cratchits’ loss.

phases.label: Seller & fence
phases.note: She sells him things taken from a dead man’s room.
